In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
synchronous MPC protocols are faster and more efficient than asynchronous ones.

synchronous MPC protocols are optimal with regard to the corruption threshold and input freedom but are not robust against network asynchrony, whereas asynchronous MPC protocols are robust against network asynchonry but cannot achieve the optimal corruption thresholds or input freedom.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a protocol that is secure in both synchronous and asynchronous settings.
we present a fully secure asynchronous synchronous MPC protocol that tolerates up to n/3 corrupted parties.
we provide a protocol for secure synchronous MPC with asynchronous fallback.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the above two communication models are not necessarily in conflict.

it is always possible to securely compute any functionality, even when the network is fully asychronous, as long as the underlying MPC protocol is secure in a synchronous network with a sufficiently high bound on the network delay.
it is possible to combine the benefits of both models, and obtain protocols that are secure under both conditions.
